title: Your Chance to Own a Piece of India's Stock Market: The NSE IPO Explained
description: The National Stock Exchange (NSE), where many Indian stocks are traded, is launching its Initial Public Offering (IPO) soon. This means for the first time, yo.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for retail investors in the NSE IPO?
faq.a: Retail investors will need to bid for a minimum of 8 shares, which at the upper price band of ₹1,785 per share, would mean a minimum investment of ₹14,280 (8 shares * ₹1,785).

faq.q: When will the NSE shares be listed on the stock market?
faq.a: The shares are expected to be listed on September 24, 2026.

faq.q: Why has the IPO size been reduced from earlier estimates?
faq.a: The proposed offer size has been reduced because some existing shareholders, including public-sector insurance companies and Morgan Stanley, have opted to sell fewer shares than they initially planned.

faq.q: Is this the first time a stock exchange is listing in India?
faq.a: No, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is already a listed entity. However, the NSE IPO is significant due to its size and market dominance.

faq.q: Who are the main shareholders selling shares in this IPO?
faq.a: Several existing shareholders are participating in the Offer for Sale, including State Bank of India and Morgan Stanley Strategic (Mauritius), among others.
